column11: Megillah 16b: ‘§ The Gemara returns to its explanation of the Megilla. The verse states: “The Jews had light and gladness, and joy and honor” (Esther 8:16). column11: Bava Batra 10b: ‘It is taught in a baraita: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai said to his students: My sons, what is the meaning of that which the verse states: “Righteousness exalts a nation, but the kindness of the peoples is sin” (Proverbs 14:34)? column13: Therefore, in that transcendent realm above time, evil holds no true existence for Israel, and combining sinful intent with deed cannot occur there. column11: Megillah 7b: ‘Rava said: A Purim feast that one ate at night did not fulfill his obligation. Rav Ashi said to him: What is the reason that the Sages did not come today? Rav Kahana answered: Perhaps they are preoccupied with the Purim feast. Rav Ashi said to him: Wasn’t it possible for them to eat the feast at night on Purim, instead of being derelict in their Torah study on Purim day? Rav Kahana said to him: Didn’t the master learn that which Rava said: A Purim feast that one ate at night did not fulfill his obligation? Rav Ashi said to him: Did Rava say that? column11: Megillah 16b: ‘§ The Gemara returns to its explanation of the Megilla. The verse states: “The Jews had light and gladness, and joy and honor” (Esther 8:16). Rav Yehuda said: “Light”; this is referring to the Torah that they once again studied. And similarly it says: “For the mitzva is a lamp and the Torah is light” (Proverbs 6:23). “Gladness” [simḥa]; this is referring to the Festivals that they once again observed. And similarly it says: “And you shall be glad [vesamakhta] on your Festival” (Deuteronomy 16:14). “Joy” [sasson]; this is referring to circumcision, as they once again circumcised their sons. And similarly it says: “I rejoice [sas] at Your word” (Psalms 119:162), which the Sages understood as referring to David’s rejoicing over the mitzva of circumcision.’ Context and connection to Machshavot Charutz: In Machshavot Charutz 6, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Megillah 16b) to illuminate his exposition here (“And "and gladness" (Esther 8:16)—this is circumcision (Megillah 16b), meaning the perfection of character traits whose root and culmination reside in Yesod; for this is their primary perfection:...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the supernal levels of Thought (Machshavah), the rectification of human desire and intellect, and the inner light of the Oral Torah developed in Machshavot Charutz.

column15: “And they journeyed from Rephidim, and came to the wilderness of Sinai” (Exodus 19:2)—on which the Gemara (Bekhorot 5b) expounds that at Rephidim they slackened their hands from the words of Torah. column11: Ecclesiastes 7:20: ‘For there is not one good person on earth who does what is best and doesn’t err.’ Context and connection to Machshavot Charutz: In Machshavot Charutz 6, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Ecclesiastes 7:20) to illuminate his exposition here (“for "there is not a righteous man upon earth that does good, and sins not" (Koheles 7:20); except that for the Jews this unfolded: that "Your people are all righteous" (Yeshayah 60:21), the...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the supernal levels of Thought (Machshavah), the rectification of human desire and intellect, and the inner light of the Oral Torah developed in Machshavot Charutz.
